record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.original_question: How should massive machine-type communication (mMTC) be supported in cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) when many low-complexity devices transmit sporadically with very small packets, strict latency and reliability requirements, limited channel-coherence resources for orthogonal pilots, uncertain traffic patterns, and insufficient or costly channel state information?

evidence.quote: The accommodation of mMTC traffic in cellular networks brings new fundamental challenges [131].

As a consequence, in the massive MTC context, the signaling overhead makes many conventional techniques almost useless and new approaches to random access and the control plane, or even the data transmission, are required.
These are unsolved challenges that call for new solution techniques.

While approaches in the literature assume the availability of full or partial channel state information [133], in mMTC setups, the acquisition of channel state information requires the allocation of additional resources and it is also possible the assumed channel models do not capture the real characteristics of the transmission channels.

artifact.category_tag: cell-free massive MIMO and massive machine-type communications
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a broad open research challenge in the wireless-communications literature. Recent surveys and research papers (2023–2025) on grant-free and unsourced random access for cell-free massive MIMO continue to identify activity detection, pilot design, and CSI acquisition for mMTC in CF-MMIMO as unresolved, with only partial results for specific subproblems (e.g., AMP-based activity detection, covariance-based detection, unsourced random access bounds). No comprehensive solution meeting all stated requirements is reported.

status_evidence.title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies massive access for mMTC in CF-MMIMO as an open challenge requiring new techniques.
status_evidence.claim: The overall design problem is explicitly listed as an open research challenge.

status_evidence.title: Grant-Free Access for Cell-Free Massive MIMO (recent surveys)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent works study activity detection and unsourced random access in cell-free MIMO but address only subsets of the requirements (no joint latency/reliability/CSI-cost guarantees).
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results exist for components of the framework.
